_comment_file: Every failure the core can hand the interface, keyed by the stable `code` on `IpcError`. The codes are raised all over `crates/remoter-ipc` — error.rs, session.rs, sftp.rs, tunnel.rs, commands.rs, state.rs, bridge.rs, vault_admin.rs, import.rs, recents.rs, audit.rs — and `src/i18n/failures.catalogue.test.ts` reads every one of those files, so a code with no entry here is a failing build rather than a sentence that turns up in English months later. The code is the join: the core sends a code, a sentence, an optional diagnostic and an ordered list of next actions, and this file supplies the sentence and the actions in the reader's language. Six rules for anyone editing this file. (1) `actions` is positional: the order is the order the core offered, and a label is used only when the entry has one at that position. (2) The `action` object at the end of this file is the shared lexicon, keyed by what the action means rather than by the failure it belongs to. Two kinds of entry rely on it and carry no `actions` of their own: every `session.*` failure, whose actions the core composes from a fixed set (`action_text` in session.rs) in an order that depends on what actually failed; and a code the core raises from several places with a different button each time, where one positional label would be the wrong sentence for every other arm. The lexicon labels those by the sentence the core sent. Positional labels still win where an entry has them. (3) No sentence here may quote a password, a passphrase, a key or any other secret — a failure is the one moment an implementation is tempted to say what it was given. (4) The sentences carry no placeholders. The core fills its own sentence with the specifics (a path, a slot number, a byte offset) and those cannot be recovered from the finished string, so each sentence here is written to stay true without them; an English reader is shown the core's own sentence, specifics and all, and every other language is shown this one. (5) A message says what failed and what the reader can do about it. 'An error occurred' is never an acceptable translation of anything below. (6) A few entries deliberately carry no `message` at all, and say so in a `_comment_`: for those the core composes the only description of what happened, so the reader is shown that sentence rather than a generalisation of it.

unknown._comment_: Not a code the core sends: `asFailure` in apps/desktop/ui/src/lib/ipc.ts uses it when a rejection arrives with no shape at all — a panic inside a command, or a transport failure below Tauri. It is the last sentence in the application and should never be reached.

locked.message: No vault is open. Unlock one to see your connections.

auto-locked.message: The vault locked itself after the idle period you set. Unlock it to carry on.

locked-by-trigger.message: The vault locked itself because an event you chose to lock on happened. Unlock it to carry on.
actions: Change what locks it in vault settings

vault._comment_unlock-failed: SECURITY-CRITICAL. This sentence must not say which factor was wrong, and a translation must not add that either: before a key slot has unwrapped the master key, naming the password or the key file as the wrong one tells an attacker which half they have already guessed. See the module docs in crates/remoter-ipc/src/error.rs.

unlock-failed.message: That did not unlock the vault.
actions: Check the key file, if this vault uses one

header-tampered.message: The header of this vault has been modified since it was written, so its contents cannot be trusted.
actions: Open a backup beside the vault
Check whether a sync client rewrote the file

body-corrupt.message: The contents of this vault could not be decrypted. The file is damaged.
actions: Open a backup beside the vault
Check the drive the vault is stored on

no-such-method.message: This vault does not offer that unlock method.
actions: Choose one of the methods this vault offers

vault._comment_fido2-unsupported: The core sends this code both when a hardware key is offered as a way in and when one is added as a key slot, so the sentence has to stay true of both. It has no `actions` of its own for the same reason: the two arms offer differently worded buttons, and the shared `action` lexicon at the end of this file labels whichever one the core sent.

fido2-unsupported.message: Hardware key unlock is not implemented in this version of Remoter.

not-a-vault.message: That file is not a Remoter vault.

unsupported-format.message: That vault uses a vault format version this build of Remoter does not read.

corrupt.message: This vault is damaged: its structure could not be read.
actions: Open a backup beside the vault

corrupt-row.message: This vault holds a record this build of Remoter cannot read.
actions: Open a backup beside the vault

header-encode.message: The header for this vault could not be encoded, so it was not written.
actions: Report this — the vault on disk is unchanged

crypto.message: A cryptographic step on this vault failed, so the operation was abandoned.

kdf-too-weak.message: Those Argon2id parameters are below the floor Remoter accepts, and a weaker vault is not an acceptable trade for a faster unlock.

kdf-params-refused.message: This vault declares Argon2id parameters above anything this build will attempt. Nothing was derived.
actions: Open the vault on the machine that wrote it
Open a backup beside the vault

no-such-slot.message: This vault has no such key slot.

no-slot-of-kind.message: This vault has no slot of that kind.

slot-table-full.message: This vault already holds the maximum number of key slots.

last-slot.message: That is the only way into this vault; removing it would lock you out permanently.

wrong-slot-kind.message: That key slot is of another kind, so the operation does not apply to it.
actions: Choose a slot of the right kind

slot-credential-missing.message: That key slot cannot be re-wrapped without its password, and dropping it silently would take away someone's way in. Nothing was changed.
actions: Enter the password for that slot
Drop that slot from the rotation deliberately

slot-credential-rejected.message: That does not open the key slot, so the slot was left exactly as it was.
actions: Check the key file, if that slot uses one

keychain.message: This machine's credential store is unavailable, or holds no token for this vault.

recovery-key-malformed.message: That is not a recovery key: a recovery key is fourteen groups of four characters.
actions: Check you pasted the whole key

recovery-key-checksum.message: That recovery key looks mistyped — its check group does not match the rest.
actions: Compare it against the copy you saved

keyfile.message: The key file could not be read.
actions: Check the file is where it was when the vault was created
Mount the drive it lives on

database.message: The database inside this vault rejected the operation.
actions: Open a backup beside the vault

schema-too-new.message: This vault was written by a newer version of Remoter: its schema version is one this build does not understand.

migration-failed.message: This vault could not be migrated to the newer schema; the file was left as it was.
actions: Open a backup beside the vault
Type a name for this vault

vault._comment_password-empty: The core raises this both for a vault's master password and for a key slot's password, so the sentence has to stay true of both.

password-empty.message: That password is empty, and nothing can be derived from an empty one.

vault._comment_password-too-weak: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The refusal must keep its reason: a weak password is not rescued by the key derivation function, and a vault is only as strong as its weakest slot. A translation that softens this into 'consider a stronger password' invites the user to keep the one they typed.

password-too-weak.message: That password is too easy to guess, and a vault is only as strong as its weakest slot. Argon2id raises the cost of every guess, but it cannot rescue a password an attacker tries early.
actions: Use a longer, less predictable password

kdf-upgrade-refused.message: That does not open the slot that needs strengthening, so the slot was left exactly as it was.
actions: Enter the password this vault was created with
Leave it for now — the vault still opens

vault._comment_locked-unsaved: SECURITY-CRITICAL in the data-loss sense: the vault is safe, the keys are gone from memory, and unsaved changes are gone with them. A translation must keep both facts. Do not imply the changes can be recovered.

locked-unsaved.message: The vault is locked and its keys are wiped, but the file could not be written, so anything changed since the last successful save is gone.
actions: Check the drive or share the vault is stored on
Unlock it again and check what is missing

vault._comment_unlock-throttled: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Like vault.unlock-failed, this sentence must not say which factor was wrong. It must also keep its reassurance: the wait is a delay, not a lockout, and a translation that reads like the vault has been sealed will send people looking for their recovery key when they do not need it.

unlock-throttled.message: Too many unlock attempts in a row did not work, so the next one waits. Nothing has been locked out: the vault opens as soon as the wait is over.
actions: Check the key file, if this vault uses one

invalid._comment_: A bug in the interface, not something the reader did: the frontend sent the core a field it cannot read. Keep the sentence blameless and keep the action pointing at a bug report.
invalid.message: A value in that request is not usable.
actions: Report this — the interface sent something the core cannot read

failed.message: That file could not be read or written.
actions: Check the path exists and is writable

csprng.message: The operating system's random number generator is unavailable, so nothing random can be generated safely.

not-a-private-key.message: That file is not a private key. A public key, a certificate or an unrelated file cannot authenticate a connection.
actions: Choose the private key rather than its .pub companion
Use the platform SSH agent instead

key._comment_unsupported-format: The refusal is a real limitation, not a conversion the user can perform: no protocol in this build can authenticate with a key of that kind, so the actions must not suggest converting the file. The three algorithm names in the first action are algorithm names, not words; leave them exactly as they are.

unsupported-format.message: That is a private key of a kind no protocol in this build can authenticate with. Nothing was written.
actions: Use an Ed25519, ECDSA or RSA key instead
Use the platform SSH agent instead

key._comment_legacy-encrypted: Different from unsupported-format: the key itself is fine, it is the PEM container that is encrypted, and Remoter has to read the container before it can store the key. The first action quotes two commands. Translate the sentence around them if there is one; never translate the commands themselves, and keep `<file>` and `<copy>` exactly as they are. The word 'copy' is load-bearing: `ssh-keygen -p` rewrites the file it is given, and the user's key file is very often shared with other tools.

legacy-encrypted.message: That key is encrypted inside its own PEM container, and Remoter has to be able to read the container before it can store the key. Nothing was written.
actions: Use the platform SSH agent instead

passphrase-required.message: That key is passphrase-protected, and without the passphrase Remoter cannot use it to authenticate.
actions: Choose a key that is not passphrase-protected

key._comment_passphrase-rejected: Distinct from passphrase-required, which is what a key gets when no passphrase was supplied at all. This one means the passphrase was actually tried against the container and did not open it. None of these key containers authenticates the passphrase, so a corrupt file produces the same observation; the sentence names the likelier of the two because it is the one the reader can act on. Do not soften it into "may not" — the passphrase was tried.

passphrase-rejected.message: That passphrase does not open the key. Nothing was written.
actions: Check the passphrase and try again
Use the platform SSH agent instead

key._comment_passphrase-not-needed: The reader typed a passphrase for a key whose container says the key material is not enciphered. This is a mismatch to point out, not a fault to report: the second action assumes they may have picked the wrong one of two key files. The refusal never quotes what was typed.

passphrase-not-needed.message: That key is not passphrase-protected, so the passphrase would open nothing. Nothing was written.
actions: Store this key without a passphrase
Choose the passphrase-protected key you meant

key._comment_passphrase-uncheckable: Not a wrong passphrase and not an unusable key: Remoter can store and connect with keys it cannot check the passphrase of, and refuses to store the passphrase for exactly that reason. The first action quotes two commands. Translate the sentence around them if there is one; never translate the commands themselves, and keep `<file>` and `<copy>` exactly as they are. The word 'copy' is load-bearing: `ssh-keygen -p` rewrites the file it is given, and the user's key file is very often shared with other tools. The diagnostic beside this sentence names which container could not be opened.

passphrase-uncheckable.message: Remoter cannot open that key's container to check the passphrase, so it will not store one it cannot vouch for. Nothing was written.
actions: Use the platform SSH agent instead

not-a-private-key.message: That item is not a credential holding a private key, so there is no key to read or replace on it.
actions: Choose a key file for it first

purpose-refused.message: That credential's restriction does not cover what it was about to be used for, so the vault refused to open it. Widen the restriction in the credential's settings, or choose a credential that already allows that use.

node._comment_not-found: Sent both for an item missing from the vault and for one missing from the tree on screen. Either way the item is gone and the tree on screen is stale, which is what the sentence says.

not-found.message: That item is no longer in the tree; it was probably deleted in another window.

parent-not-found.message: The folder you dropped that into no longer exists.

duplicate.message: An item with that identifier is already in the tree.

not-a-container.message: Only folders can hold other items.

cycle.message: A folder cannot be moved inside itself.

too-deep.message: That move would nest the tree deeper than the limit allows.

parent-changed.message: An edit cannot re-parent an item; move it instead.
actions: Drag it to the new folder

not-a-connection.message: Only connections have resolved settings to show.

node._comment_field-not-applicable: No `actions` of its own: the core raises this from seven places with a different instruction each time — select a credential, create one, edit the connection, edit a folder — so a label at position 0 would be the wrong sentence six times out of seven. The shared `action` lexicon at the end of this file translates each of them by what the core actually sent.

field-not-applicable.message: That field does not apply to this kind of item.

corrupt.message: The item tree in this vault does not terminate: a parent chain loops.

not-found.message: That credential has no such secret stored.

too-large.message: That file is larger than this build reads. Nothing was parsed.

malformed-xml.message: That file is not well-formed XML.

Export the file again from the application that wrote it

Export it again from the application that wrote it

Re-save it from a newer version of the source application

Export it again from the application that wrote it

too-many-nodes.message: That file would create more items than the limit allows.

unknown-format.message: That file is not in a format Remoter imports: it is not an mRemoteNG document, an OpenSSH config or a CSV export.

orphaned-nodes.message: That file produced items whose folder is not in the import, so the tree could not be built. Nothing was written.

no-such-preview.message: That import preview is no longer held: it was committed, cancelled, or dropped when the vault locked. Nothing was written.

validation._comment_file: The reader's own input being wrong. Each sentence names the rule rather than the value, because the core has already put the value in the sentence it sends and this one has to read correctly without it.

invalid-port.message: This connection has no usable port. Open its settings and set one between 1 and 65535.

gateway-cycle.message: The gateway chain loops back on itself: one of its hops appears in the chain twice.

gateway-too-long.message: This gateway chain has more hops than Remoter will walk.

gateway-deleted.message: A hop in this gateway chain refers to a connection that has been deleted.

gateway-credential-required.message: A hop in this gateway chain has no credential to authenticate with.

limit.message: You have as many sessions open as the limit allows. Close one, or raise the limit in settings.

credential-deleted.message: The credential this connection used was deleted. Choose another, or enter one now.

credential-purpose.message: This credential is restricted to other uses and cannot be used here.

credential-required.message: No credential is available for this connection, and SSH has no anonymous login.

credential-no-username.message: That credential has no account name, and SSH has no anonymous login.

credential-not-a-credential.message: What this connection points at is not a credential, so it cannot be used to sign in.

credential-external.message: That credential is held by another provider, and this build has no plugin that can fetch it.

credential-unsupported.message: That credential is a certificate, which sessions of this protocol do not use.

dns.message: That address could not be resolved. Check the name, or your DNS.

refused.message: The server refused the connection. Is the service running?

timeout.message: The server did not respond in time. Check the firewall, or the gateway.

unreachable.message: That address is unreachable from this machine. Check the network.

hop-failed.message: The target could not be reached through the gateway chain: one of its hops failed. The details say which, and why.

io.message: The connection failed on a read or a write. The details say which.

host-key-unknown.message: The server offered a host key Remoter has never seen, and the session could not ask about it.

session._comment_host-key-changed: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The reader decides from this sentence whether to trust the server in front of them, and a changed host key is what an interception looks like (docs/security/threat-model.md, T3). A translation must keep all three parts: the key is not the one that was trusted, this can mean someone is intercepting, and the two keys are in the details. Do not soften it into a routine warning, and do not suggest accepting the key.

host-key-changed.message: The key this server offered is not the one Remoter trusts for it. This can mean someone is intercepting the connection. The details show the trusted key and the one that was offered.

host-key-rejected.message: The key the server offered was not accepted, so the session did not continue.

host-key-nothing-to-replace.message: Nothing is stored for this host yet, so there is no key to replace. Review the fingerprint and accept it, or decline.

fingerprint-malformed.message: That is not a SHA-256 fingerprint, so it could not be compared with the one the server offered.

confirmation-mismatch.message: That is not the confirmation shown on screen, so the stored host key was left alone.

no-shared-algorithm.message: The server only offers algorithms Remoter no longer accepts. The details list them.

session._comment_certificate-untrusted: SECURITY-CRITICAL. This is the sentence a reader decides from when a server's certificate cannot be validated. A translation must keep the last clause: until the reason is resolved, there is no proof this is the intended server. Do not soften it, and do not imply the session may be continued safely.

certificate-untrusted.message: The certificate this server offered is not trusted. The details say why. Until that is resolved, there is no proof this is the server you meant to reach.

handshake-failed.message: The handshake did not complete, so the session did not open. The details say how far it got.

trust-store.message: The vault could not record the host key decision, so it was not saved.

auth-method-unavailable.message: The server does not accept that authentication method. The details list the ones it offers.

auth-cancelled.message: The sign-in was cancelled, so the session did not open.

agent-unavailable.message: The SSH agent is not running, or this process cannot reach its socket.

setting-invalid.message: One of this connection's settings is not usable. The details say which, and what it has to be.

setting-required.message: One of this connection's settings has no value, and the connection cannot open without it.

protocol-unsupported.message: Nothing in this build speaks that connection's protocol, or it cannot do what was asked of it.

unsupported.message: Sessions of this protocol do not support that.

protocol-violation.message: The server sent something the protocol does not allow.

session._comment_path-not-found: A file-manager failure on a session that is connected and working. It used to be reported as `setting-invalid`, which sent the reader to the connection editor to fix a setting that was never wrong. Keep the second sentence: the commonest cause by far is a listing that is a few seconds out of date, and the way out is to read the folder again.

path-not-found.message: There is nothing at that path on the server. It may have been moved, renamed or deleted since this folder was last read.

session._comment_path-permission-denied: SECURITY-ADJACENT. This must not read as a sign-in failure. It used to be reported as `auth-rejected` — 'the server rejected these credentials' — on a connection that had authenticated minutes earlier, which sends the reader off to re-check an SSH key that is working. The distinction between 'who you are' and 'what this file allows' is the whole sentence; a translation that blurs it undoes the fix.

path-permission-denied.message: The server refused access to that path. This is a file-permission refusal, not a sign-in problem: the connection is authenticated, and this account does not have permission for this file or folder.

session._comment_file-operation-refused: HONESTY. SFTP version 3 has one catch-all status for everything that is not 'missing' or 'not permitted', so a full disk, a quota, a read-only mount, a lock and a cross-device rename are genuinely indistinguishable here. The sentence names the likely causes and admits it cannot tell them apart; do not turn it into a guess at one of them.

file-operation-refused.message: The server could not complete that operation on this file and did not say why. A full disk, a quota, a read-only filesystem, a lock, or a rename across two filesystems all arrive in exactly this form.

cancelled.message: The session was cancelled before it opened.

closed.message: That session is no longer running.

no-such-session.message: That session is not open any more. Its tab can be closed.

no-such-node.message: That connection is not in this vault any more. It may have been deleted in another window.

no-such-prompt.message: That host key question is no longer open. The session may have given up waiting.

frozen.message: The vault is locked, and this vault's policy is to freeze session input until it is unlocked. The session is still connected.

event-stream-closed.message: The session's output stream was closed before the session was, so it has been ended.

task-failed.message: The session failed with an internal error and has been closed. Nothing else was affected.

shutdown-timeout.message: The session did not shut down in time and was stopped by force. This is a defect worth reporting.

internal.message: Remoter hit an internal error. This is a defect worth reporting.

failed._comment_: Deliberately has no `message`. The core composes this one at the moment of failure — it is a diagnostic sentence naming what went wrong, with no `detail` beside it — so a generalised translation here would replace the only account of what happened. The reader sees the core's English sentence and translated action buttons. If SessionFailureDto ever carries the taxonomy code instead of this wrapper, give this entry a message and remove the note.

session-not-ready.message: That session is not connected, so there is nothing to browse on it yet. A file pane opens on a connection that has already authenticated.

directory-not-empty.message: That directory was not removed. A directory has to be empty before it can be removed, and this one may not be.

transfer-running.message: That transfer has not finished, so there is nothing to retry about it yet.

sftp._comment_unsafe-name: The name in question came from the remote server. The point of the sentence is that Remoter refused to take the server's word for where a file should land; a translation must not turn it into a complaint about the user's choice of folder.

unsafe-name.message: That file cannot be saved into that folder: the name the server gave it is not a plain file name.
actions: Choose a name for it yourself

no-such-pane.message: That file pane is not open any more. Its session may have ended.

no-such-transfer.message: That transfer is not in this pane's queue.

subsystem-unavailable.message: This server did not open an SFTP subsystem. Some servers have it switched off, and some restrict it to particular accounts.
actions: Ask the server's administrator to enable the SFTP subsystem

listing-too-large.message: That directory holds more than Remoter will read in one listing.
actions: Use the terminal for this directory

rename-failed.message: That file could not be renamed. A rename cannot cross a filesystem on most servers, and one that tries is refused exactly like this.
actions: Copy it across and delete the original
Rename it within the same filesystem

sftp._comment_local-destination-unreadable: Raised while checking, before a transfer is queued, whether something is already at the place a download would write. It is deliberately not fatal: the transfer is still offered, and the dialog says which destinations could not be looked at. 'Nothing is there' and 'nobody could look' are different answers and the interface must not show the first when it means the second.

local-destination-unreadable.message: Remoter could not check whether a file is already at that place on this computer. The transfer can still be sent, but nothing is known about what it would replace.

transfer-failed._comment_: Deliberately has no `message`, for the same reason as session.failed: the sentence is the transfer's own diagnostic, composed when it failed, and there is no detail beside it to fall back on.

clipboard._comment_unavailable: The system clipboard, used by the terminal's copy and paste. The core never logs what the clipboard held.

unavailable.message: The system clipboard could not be reached, so nothing was copied or pasted.

clipboard._comment_too-large: The limit protects a remote shell from receiving megabytes of text as keystrokes by accident. The second action points at the file manager, which is the right tool for moving a file.

too-large.message: The clipboard holds more text than a terminal paste will send. Nothing was pasted.
actions: Transfer the file over SFTP instead

no-such-tunnel.message: That tunnel is not open any more.

tunnel._comment_bind-exposed: SECURITY-CRITICAL. This is the sentence that stands between a forward bound to localhost and one the whole local network can use. A translation must keep both halves: the address is not loopback, and the forward would therefore be reachable from the local network. Do not soften it into a note about a preference.

bind-exposed.message: That is not a loopback address, so this forward would be reachable from the local network. Tick the option that says so, or bind it to localhost.

tunnel._comment_host-key-unknown: SECURITY-CRITICAL. A tunnel has no window in which to ask about an unknown host key, so the sentence sends the reader to a session where the fingerprint can be reviewed. A translation must not suggest the key can be accepted from here, and must keep the instruction to review the fingerprint.

host-key-unknown.message: That server offered a host key Remoter has not been told to trust, and a tunnel has no window to ask in. Open a session to it first, review the fingerprint, and accept it there.
actions: Open a session to this connection

keyfile._comment_unprotected: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The refusal exists because a key file that every account on the machine can read is not a second factor at all. A translation must keep the reason and the consequence — it was not written — and must not present this as a permissions warning the user may wave away.

unprotected.message: That key file cannot be restricted to your account: the file system it is on does not carry permissions, so every account on this machine could read it. A key file anyone can read is not a second factor, so it was not written.
actions: Choose a location on a disk that keeps file permissions
Encrypt the removable drive, then write the key file to it

label-empty.message: A key slot needs a name, so the list can say which key this is.
actions: Type a name for this slot

terminal-reserved.message: That combination belongs to the remote host: a focused terminal has to receive it, so binding it here would stop it reaching the shell.
actions: Bind it as an application shortcut, reached through the terminal prefix

export-encode.message: The audit entries could not be encoded, so nothing was written.

encode.message: The recent-vault list could not be encoded, so it was not written.
Your settings could not be encoded, so they were not saved.

_comment_action: The shared action lexicon: one entry per action sentence that cannot be labelled where the failure is, translated once. Two kinds of action end up here: the ones the core composes for a session failure (`action_text` in session.rs), which turn up under dozens of codes in an order that depends on what failed; and the ones belonging to a code the core raises from several places with a different button each time, where a label at a fixed position would be the wrong sentence for every other arm. `src/i18n/failures.ts` holds the English sentence for each key and looks an action up here when the failure's own entry has no label at that position; `failures.catalogue.test.ts` checks that list against the Rust, so a wording change there fails the build here. These are button labels: keep them short, and keep them in the imperative or verbal-noun form the rest of this file uses.
